label: Species richness
blurb: The most biodiverse and species-rich places (CDFW ACE; Kling et al. 2019) and how much of each lies in 30x30 (report Tables 9–11).

charts.title: Most species-rich areas by taxon
charts.subtitle: ACE richness: top 20% (native) or top 5% (rare, endemic) of California's hexagons (report Table 10)

method: ACE (CDFW Areas of Conservation Emphasis v3) features are defined as in the report: rank 5 for the BioRank and Rare Rank indices; for per-taxon richness, ACE hexagons at or above California's 80th percentile (native richness) or 95th percentile (rare and endemic richness). Thresholds are always computed over all of California's hexagons, so a feature means the same thing in any area. Plant richness and rarity-weighted endemic plant richness are Kling et al. (2019), statewide top 20%. These features sit on coarser grids (ACE hexagons; resolution-8 H3 cells, about 180 acres); within them, conservation status comes from each resolution-10 land cell. Like the report, these value-based features get no need class: a network that protects the richest places should hold more than its share of them.
